subject: Dedicated capacity commitment phasing + burn forecast — ZephyrTech
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Shah <aisha.shah@zephyrtech.com>
Cc: Diego Ramos <diego.ramos@zephyrtech.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity commitment phasing + burn forecast — ZephyrTech

Hi Aisha / Diego,

Thanks again for the time today — this note summarizes three dedicated reservation options that map to the usage profile you shared (steady query load with two predictable spikes for batch indexing). I attached a short deck and a burn forecast workbook.

High-level options (attached PDF has the full table):
- Anchor: 16 GPUs minimum, steady-state for production inference, burst pool for index windows. Ramp over 2 months.
- Staircase: 8 GPUs baseline with scheduled activation windows to cover indexing spikes; scale to 24 GPUs during peak weeks. Ramp in 30/60/90 day tranches.
- Flexible Block: 12 GPU committed floor with 40% burst credit and an activation SLA for short bursts up to 48 hours. Shortest commitment, best near-term capital efficiency.

I included a conservative token burn forecast in the spreadsheet so you can see how unit cost changes by quantization and batching recommendations. The anchor option gives the cleanest latency SLOs; the staircase option optimizes for lower committed spend early in the contract.

Ask: Could you confirm which of the three you want us to price with a 12-month vs 24-month commit? Pricing differs materially (we can show blended unit costs). Also, if you have exact cadence for your monthly ingestion windows, send those and we’ll map warm-up windows to reduce cold-start overhead.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Kar (Karthik) and Ben to cover the technical sizing and onboarding cadence.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0113

Attachments: zephyr_dedicated_options_v2.pdf, zephyr_burn_forecast_q3-q4.xlsx

From: Aisha Shah <aisha.shah@zephyrtech.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Diego Ramos <diego.ramos@zephyrtech.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity commitment phasing + burn forecast — ZephyrTech

Thanks Sofia — helpful summary and nice level of detail. A couple of clarifying items before we pick: 

1) For the Staircase option, when you say "scheduled activation windows" — is the cost billed prorated for those windows or do we pay a full-day charge when activated? We want to avoid paying for idle capacity between short index runs.

2) For the Anchor option, what are the expected 95p latency numbers under our profile (40 token avg, mixed beam/prompt workloads)? We need a 95p < 150ms target for the web UI.

3) Can you show the impact of a 12-month vs 24-month term for each option side-by-side? 

We can do 12 months if the Staircase gives better early-month economics and the activation billing is per-hour. If it’s per-day, Leaner options look better.

I can share our indexing calendar by EOD tomorrow.

Regards,
Aisha Shah
Head of AI Platform, ZephyrTech
aisha.shah@zephyrtech.com
+1 (646) 555-2141

Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity commitment phasing + burn forecast — ZephyrTech

On Tue, May 25, 2027 at 12:03 PM, Aisha Shah <aisha.shah@zephyrtech.com> wrote:
> Thanks Sofia — helpful summary and nice level of detail. A couple of clarifying items before we pick: 
>
> 1) For the Staircase option, when you say "scheduled activation windows" — is the cost billed prorated for those windows or do we pay a full-day charge when activated?
>
> 2) For the Anchor option, what are the expected 95p latency numbers under our profile (40 token avg, mixed beam/prompt workloads)?
>
> 3) Can you show the impact of a 12-month vs 24-month term for each option side-by-side? 

Thanks for the questions — answers below. Looping Kar and Ben for any technical/detail corrections.

1) Staircase activation billing: we bill committed GPUs on a monthly pro-rated basis. For scheduled activation windows that cause us to spin up additional reserved GPUs beyond the baseline, those are billed by the hour (to the minute for metered bursts) when using our burst pool. There is a 15-minute minimum for a burst activation. This means short index runs (1–3 hrs) are charged only for the burst duration, not an entire calendar day.

2) Anchor 95p latency: With your profile and using our recommended quantization (4-bit Q4f) and batching parameters (target batch 32, dynamic batching), our bench predicts 95p token latency ~120–140ms on the Anchor 16-GPU lane at 512 context. We’ll include a microbenchmark report upon request.

3) 12 vs 24 months: pricing summary — 24 months reduces committed unit price ~18% on average; 12 months keeps flexibility but higher per-token. I attached a two-column sheet in the workbook that shows blended unit cost and total committed spend for each option and term.

Next steps proposal: you share the indexing calendar, we’ll populate a concrete ramp schedule (dates + warm-up windows) and produce a formal quote. If you want, Ben can run a quick end-to-end test in our sandbox to validate 95p latency for a sample workload.

Ben / Kar — can you confirm the 15-minute minimum burst and the 95p latency estimates? Also please add any notes on warm-up GPU wiring (prefetching KV cache) we should highlight to Zephyr.

Best,
Sofia

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Shah <aisha.shah@zephyrtech.com>, Diego Ramos <diego.ramos@zephyrtech.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity commitment phasing + burn forecast — ZephyrTech

Sofia / Kar — quick tech confirmation and a couple of internal notes I copied into the thread for the customer: 

- Confirming: burst activations are billed per-minute after a 15-minute minimum. Throttle guard ensures bursts can’t exceed 3x baseline without manual approval.
- 95p latency estimate: Ben ran a quick bench against a similar LLM profile in our staging cluster; result: 95p token latency between 118–136ms at 32-token batches and 512 context on an Anchor 16. Caveats: we used batch shaping and KV pre-warm — real-world numbers depend on prompt variability.
- Warm-up tip: for index windows, pre-warm KV cache 30–45 minutes before first heavy job; we can auto-schedule warm-up lanes as part of onboarding to avoid flash cold starts.

Attached: zephyr_burn_forecast_q3-q4.xlsx (updated with an hourly burst cost tab) and a proposal_summary_slide.png for exec review.

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachments: zephyr_burn_forecast_q3-q4.xlsx, proposal_summary_slide.png

From: Aisha Shah <aisha.shah@zephyrtech.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Diego Ramos <diego.ramos@zephyrtech.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity commitment phasing + burn forecast — ZephyrTech

Thanks — this is great and answers our immediate questions. We discussed internally and prefer the Staircase option with a 12-month term, provided the hourly burst billing and 15-minute minimum applies (that works for our indexing cadence). Please prepare a formal quote with these constraints:

- Baseline: 8 GPUs committed (monthly pro-rated)
- Ramp: 8 -> 16 GPUs in month 3, 16 -> 24 GPUs during two planned index weeks (hours metered)
- Burst: access to 3x baseline for short windows (15-minute min), hourly metering thereafter
- SLA ask: 95p token latency target < 150ms for web UI during steady-state (baseline)

We’ll send you the indexing calendar later today (Diego to attach). If you can get a quote by Tues EOD (02 Jun) we can route for procurement review. Also confirm whether we can do a test run (Ben’s sandbox) before signing.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

Best,
Aisha
